name: Anuradhapura
blurb: The first great royal and monastic city, where moonstones, guardstones and the largest stupas are at their most ambitious.

name: Polonnaruwa
blurb: The later medieval capital beside Parakrama Samudra, where the entrance carving grows busier and the Vatadage shows the whole ensemble.

name: Medirigiriya
blurb: A quiet site about 34 km from Polonnaruwa with what many consider the most intact and elegant vatadage.

name: Tiriyaya
blurb: A hilltop stupa in Trincomalee district, enlarged in the 8th century CE and later given a circular vatadage.

name: Mihintale
blurb: A sacred hill east of Anuradhapura, home to the bell-shaped Ambasthala Dagaba.

name: Sigiriya
blurb: Kashyapa I's rock citadel, with the Mirror Wall, the fresco pocket, the lion's paws and working water gardens.

name: Kala Wewa
blurb: Dhatusena's 5th-century reservoir, head of the gently falling Yodha Ela canal to Anuradhapura.

name: Kandy
blurb: The last royal capital, home to the Temple of the Tooth and a base for the painted and carved temples of the surrounding hills.

name: Embekke
blurb: A village near Kandy whose devale is famed for its carved timber pillars and brackets.

name: Jaffna (Nallur)
blurb: The northern Tamil city whose Nallur Kandaswamy Kovil is Murugan's great temple and the setting for a 25-day festival.

name: Trincomalee (Koneswaram)
blurb: An east-coast harbour town where the Shiva temple of Koneswaram stands on Swami Rock above the sea.

name: Galle Fort
blurb: A walled town on the south coast whose gate, bastions and church floor record Portuguese, Dutch and British rule.

name: Loolecondera
blurb: The estate near Kandy where James Taylor planted 19 acres of tea in 1867.

name: Hill Country (Hatton)
blurb: The tea estates around Hatton, a working landscape and home to Malaiyaha Tamil communities.
